title: Short Stuff: Lawn Darts
summary: Josh and Chuck cover lawn darts: the oversized plastic-finned darts popular in the 1970s and 1980s. They describe the game (tossing darts to land in hula hoops), the dangers (especially to young children with unfused skulls), and the history: a 1970 FDA ban, a deal with the industry to stop marketing to kids and add warnings, and a second wave of sales in sporting goods sections, sometimes bundled with volleyball sets. They trace the lawn dart's ancestor, the plumbata, a Roman-era weapon of war. They recount David Snow, an aerospace engineer whose seven-year-old daughter was fatally injured in 1987, and his activism. They explain that Consumer Product Safety Commission data, which initially mixed in regular dartboard injuries, showed more than 6,000 emergency room visits over eight years, and that the industry had broken its agreements. The CPSC voted 2-1 to ban lawn darts after a Tennessee girl was put into a coma. Today, parts can still be bought from UK companies and assembled, since the ban covers sale, not possession, and tournaments are held by a US lawn dart association.

segments.title: Opening and what lawn darts are
segments.summary: Hosts introduce lawn darts as oversized plastic-finned darts from the 1970s and 1980s, describe the hoop-toss game, and note the danger of falling darts.

segments.title: 1970 FDA ban and industry deal
segments.summary: The FDA banned lawn darts around 1970. The industry lobbied, struck a deal to stop marketing to kids, sell them in sporting goods, and add warnings.

segments.title: Second wave and plumbata ancestry
segments.summary: Lawn darts returned in the 1980s, sold in sporting goods sections and sometimes bundled with volleyball sets. The hosts describe the plumbata, an ancient weapon ancestor.

segments.title: David Snow and his daughter
segments.summary: David Snow's seven-year-old daughter was fatally injured by a lawn dart in 1987. He became a self-taught lobbyist for a ban.

segments.title: Data, industry violations, and the 1988 ban
segments.summary: CPSC data initially included regular dart injuries. Lawn dart data showed over 6,000 ER visits in eight years, and the industry had broken its agreement. The CPSC voted 2-1 to ban lawn darts after a Tennessee girl was put in a coma.

segments.title: Homemade darts, tournaments, and sign-off
segments.summary: Parts are still sold by UK companies and can be assembled since the ban covers sale, not possession. A US association holds tournaments. The hosts sign off.
